What Okyo collects, where it goes, and how to delete it

## What this policy covers

This policy explains how Okyo handles information in the mobile app and its supporting service. You can use many app features with data stored on your device. Sign-in, food analysis, idea submissions, and optional diagnostics or analytics involve the services described below. Okyo launches without in-app subscriptions or paid features. We do not sell personal information or use it for targeted advertising.

## Account and sign-in

You can create and access an Okyo account with an email address and password or Google. Apple sign-in is available when the Apple and Clerk configuration is enabled for the release. For email-and-password accounts, Clerk processes your email address and password for authentication; Okyo does not receive your password. When you use Apple or Google, that provider and Clerk process the information needed to authenticate you, such as an account identifier and any name or email address the provider shares. Clerk also processes connection and device information and can derive approximate city and country from the connection’s IP address for authentication and security. Okyo does not request GPS location. Okyo uses the resulting account session to identify your requests and manage your account. Account sessions are stored securely on your device.

## Information stored on your device

Okyo stores onboarding answers, your name and fox name, dietary preferences and allergies, nutrition targets, recipes, scan results and photos, likes, grocery selections, cooking progress, feedback, and savings estimates on your device. A scanned photo can remain in Okyo’s app storage even when you have not saved the recipe. Delete all my data in Settings removes Okyo’s local data and scan images. Removing the app also removes its local app data, subject to your device backup settings.

## Food analysis and AI

When you scan or describe food, Okyo sends the photo or text and relevant recipe context to its service. That context may include servings, cooking mode, dietary restrictions, allergies, nutrition targets, corrections, and questions you submit. The service sends the request to OpenRouter and the configured model provider to identify food, generate or revise a recipe, or answer a question. AI results, nutrition, costs, and savings are estimates. Check ingredients and allergens yourself.

## How long the photo is kept

On your device, scan photos can remain in Okyo’s app storage until you remove local data. Okyo’s service does not put the uploaded photo into its runtime database. It keeps some analysis and generated-recipe results temporarily in PostgreSQL with expiry times, and it may cache results so repeated requests can reuse them. Server backups and operational records may outlast the live entry. At the AI provider, retention is set by that provider, not by Okyo. We will not claim a provider deletes your image immediately because Okyo cannot verify that from its own code.

## Idea board

If you submit an idea, improvement, or bug report, Okyo stores the category, your message, and the submission time in PostgreSQL so the team can review it. Do not include sensitive information in a suggestion. The current idea board does not publish your submission to other users.

## Analytics and diagnostics

When enabled for a build, PostHog receives explicit app and screen activity, coarse onboarding and sign-in progress, scan outcomes, recipe actions, tour progress, settings, account-deletion outcomes, and coarse error/performance events. Properties are restricted to app version, platform, build environment, broad screen/flow categories, approved action/outcome values, and bounded durations. Okyo does not send answers, names, email addresses, account/provider IDs, session IDs, photos, recipes, allergy or health answers, signatures, typed text, IP address properties, or raw API responses. Events use a random app-generated analytics ID, not an account or app session ID; profile processing is disabled, and the ID is rotated after account deletion. The API has a separate optional PostHog integration for coarse AI-operation metrics. The app sends no automatic text capture, screenshots, or screen recordings. Sentry is separately configured for filtered crash diagnostics. When these integrations are enabled, their services also receive network connection information. Their retention settings and agreements apply.

## Subscriptions and notifications

Okyo launches without in-app subscriptions or paid features, so Apple and RevenueCat do not process Okyo purchase or entitlement data at launch. Optional cooking reminders and timers are scheduled on your device when enabled.

## Service providers and processing locations

Okyo uses Clerk for authentication, Railway and PostgreSQL for the service and its data, OpenRouter and configured model providers for AI requests, and PostHog and Sentry when those integrations are enabled. For email-and-password accounts, Clerk processes the email address and password used for authentication. Authentication providers receive connection and device information such as IP address, device/OS information, and identifiers as needed for their services. Apple and Google also process information under their own policies when you use their sign-in services. These companies may process information outside your country. Their retention practices and locations are governed by their services and agreements.

## Retention and deletion

Local app data remains until you delete it or remove the app. Temporary server analysis and recipe records expire according to the service’s configured retention periods; copies in backups may remain longer. Idea submissions and records needed for security or legal obligations may remain longer. Settings › Privacy & data lets you delete local data and request deletion of a signed-in account. You can email us for help with access or deletion requests.

## Your choices and rights

You can edit preferences and notification settings, clear local data, and delete a signed-in account in Settings. Depending on where you live, you may also have rights to access, correct, delete, or receive information about personal data and to object to some processing. Contact us to make a request; we may need to verify your identity before acting. Email us to request access to the information we hold about you.

## Children

Okyo is a general-audience cooking app and is not designed for children under 13. Do not send us personal information about a child under 13. If you believe we received such information, contact us so we can review and remove it.

## Changes to this policy

If our practices change, we will update this policy and its effective date. Material changes may also be explained in the app.

## Contact

Okyo is operated by Roberto Ferrito. For privacy questions, email Okyo at support.okyo@gmail.com.

Extra rights that may apply where you live

### Read this alongside the Privacy Policy

These notes add region-specific detail. They do not all apply to everyone — each section says who it is for. Availability depends on the countries listed in the App Store.

### A note that changes everything below

Most recipe, scan, grocery, cooking and preference data is stored on this device. Okyo supports email-and-password and Google sign-in through Clerk, and supports Apple sign-in when the Apple and Clerk configuration is enabled for the release. Clerk holds account and authentication records, including email addresses and passwords for password accounts, and Okyo’s service processes requests sent for AI features. No subscription entitlement records are collected by Okyo at launch. The in-app controls cover Okyo data on this device and signed-in account deletion; provider records may have to be handled under those providers’ own processes. Provider-controlled records are also subject to the provider’s retention and privacy practices.

### Europe and the United Kingdom (GDPR / UK GDPR)

If you are in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK you have rights to access, rectify, erase, restrict and port your personal data, to object to processing, and to complain to your data protection authority. Okyo does not use your data for automated decisions with legal effects.

### California and other US states

If you are a resident of California, Colorado, Connecticut, Virginia or another US state with a consumer privacy law, you may have rights to know, delete, correct and port your personal information, and to opt out of sale, sharing for cross-context behavioural advertising, and profiling. Okyo does not sell personal information, does not share it for targeted advertising, and does not profile you for those purposes, so there is no opt-out to offer — if that ever changes, an opt-out will be added before it does. Okyo will not discriminate against you for exercising a right.

### Washington State (My Health My Data)

Dietary restrictions, allergies and nutrition targets can count as consumer health data under Washington law. Okyo stores that information on your device and sends relevant preferences with recipe and AI requests. It does not sell this information or use it for advertising. Contact us about access or deletion.

### Canada, including Quebec

If you are in Canada you may have rights of access and correction under PIPEDA, and Quebec’s Law 25 adds further rights including portability. Contact us to exercise applicable privacy rights.

### Australia

If you are in Australia, the Australian Privacy Principles may give you rights of access and correction, and the Australian Consumer Law gives you consumer guarantees that cannot be excluded. Contact us about applicable access or correction rights.

### How to raise a request

See “Privacy requests and deletion” or contact Okyo at support.okyo@gmail.com. For account and service data, Okyo will need to verify the request using the available account and service records. Records controlled by Apple, Clerk or the AI provider may also be subject to those providers’ request processes. We may need to verify your identity before completing a request.

How to see, correct, export or delete your data

### Access — you already have it

You can view your local profile and goal in Settings, preferences in Dietary preferences and Nutrition targets, recipes in Liked, lists in Grocery, and totals in Stats & progress. Account providers and Okyo’s service also process the information described in the Privacy Policy. Contact support for access to information held by Okyo.

### Correction

Edit anything directly: your name and fox name, your goal, your dietary preferences and nutrition targets, and any generated recipe. A wrong dish result can be corrected in place without rescanning.

### Deletion

Settings › Privacy & data › Delete all my data removes every Okyo record on this device: profile and fox name, goal and onboarding answers, dietary preferences and nutrition targets, saved and generated recipes, grocery lists and checked items, Cook Mode progress, completed meals, savings and macro totals, notification preferences, your recorded permission choices, and the stored scan images. A signed-in user can also choose Delete account from that screen to remove the Clerk account record. The app prevents duplicate account-deletion requests while a request is in progress.

Okyo has no purchase records to remove at launch. Uninstalling Okyo also removes the app’s stored data.

### Export

For a copy of information held by Okyo, contact the support email in this policy. We may need to verify your identity. Provider-controlled records may require a request to that provider.

### Objection and consent withdrawal

You can turn notifications, camera access and photo access off in your device Settings, or turn notification categories off inside Okyo. Analytics is controlled by the publisher’s build configuration, not by an in-app toggle; it sends events only when the PostHog integration is enabled. Okyo does not use analytics for advertising or cross-app tracking.

### Opting out of sale or targeted advertising

There is nothing to opt out of. Okyo does not sell personal information and does not share it for targeted advertising.

### If you would rather talk to a person

For privacy questions, email Okyo at support.okyo@gmail.com. Signed-in accounts can be deleted in the app. A person requesting help with a third-party account record may need to contact that provider directly.

## How long Okyo keeps things

Retention for each kind of data

### On this device

Your profile, preferences, nutrition targets, recipes, grocery lists, cooking progress, completed meals and totals stay on this device until you delete them or remove the app. Okyo does not expire them on a timer.

### Scan photos on this device

A photo you scan is copied into Okyo’s app storage and can remain there even when the recipe is not saved. Okyo may remove an uncommitted scan when it can identify that scan session, but this is not the retention guarantee. “Delete all my data” removes the whole scan-image folder.

### On the Okyo service

The service keeps temporary analysis context for up to 15 minutes, generated-recipe working records for up to 24 hours, result caches for up to 24 hours, and rejected-image result caches for up to 1 hour. Production working records use PostgreSQL with expiry times; expired records are no longer served and are removed by cleanup. The runtime database excludes uploaded image bytes. Operational records and backups may remain longer.

### Logs

Operational log entries record what happened — sizes, models, outcomes — with image data, meal descriptions and correction text stripped out. Hosting providers retain operational records under their configured retention settings and agreements.

### At the AI provider

AI-provider retention depends on the provider and the applicable service agreements. Okyo does not promise immediate deletion by an external provider.

### Purchases

Okyo does not collect subscription or purchase records at launch. If paid features are introduced later, the store and any enabled entitlement provider will have their own retention rules.

Who else touches your data, and why

### AI provider — OpenRouter

Receives the food photo or dish description, plus recipe context such as servings, cooking mode and your dietary preferences, and routes it to the model Okyo has configured so a dish can be identified and a recipe written. This is a service provider acting on Okyo’s instructions for that purpose. The model vendor behind the routing is a further processor in the same chain.

### App Store distribution — Apple

Apple distributes Okyo through the App Store. No Okyo payment or subscription processing is enabled at launch. Apple is an independent party with its own privacy policy.

### Future entitlement checks — RevenueCat

RevenueCat is not enabled for Okyo at launch. If subscriptions are introduced later, Okyo may enable it to check store entitlements without receiving your recipes, photos or dietary information.

### Authentication and optional diagnostics

Clerk processes account, sign-in, connection and device information, including approximate location derived from IP address. PostHog receives limited product events when enabled; Sentry receives sanitized error reports when enabled. Their handling is described in the Privacy Policy.

### What is not here

No advertising network, marketing or email platform, or data broker is integrated. Analytics transmission is disabled unless the publisher deliberately enables the PostHog configuration for the app build or API service. The event limits and data types are described in the Privacy Policy.

### Hosting

Railway hosts Okyo’s API and PostgreSQL working records. Hosting, backup and operational retention follow the service configuration and provider agreements. Processing may occur outside your country.
